skills.name: Prepositions of place, movement and manner

note.text: Prepositions show relationships. At and in can locate a person; to commonly marks a destination; into and out of express movement across a boundary. Through describes movement within and across something; across often describes movement from one side to another. Travel by bus differs from on foot. Context determines the phrase, and a preposition's meaning cannot be learned by replacing every one with to. Use complete examples and check the relationship intended.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Bih waits at the bus stop, travels to Buea and walks into a room. She travels by bus but goes on foot for the short final walk. The phrases identify position, destination, boundary crossing and manner. They are original model sentences, not instructions to travel without an adult or a real timetable.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Ask whether the sentence describes location, direction or method. Choose a phrase that matches the whole sentence. Do not confuse into, which shows movement, with in, which can describe a position. Check fixed expressions such as on foot.

key_words.meaning: where a person or object is
the endpoint towards which movement is directed
movement from outside to inside or inside to outside
the means or method of a journey

examples: Bih is at the bus stop.
Bih walks into the reading room.

mistake.wrong: At the stop necessarily means she has already travelled to another town.
mistake.right: location: where a person or object is.
mistake.why: The phrase locates her; it does not state a journey's destination.

wrong.text: At the stop necessarily means she has already travelled to another town.
wrong.explain: The phrase locates her; it does not state a journey's destination.

wrong.text: To Buea describes only the colour of the bus.
wrong.explain: To introduces the destination, not a physical property.

wrong.text: Into and in always express exactly the same movement.
wrong.explain: Into emphasises entry across the boundary; in can describe a position.

wrong.text: By foot is the standard school expression required for walking.
wrong.explain: The standard expression is on foot; by is used in by bus.
